prose_updates.tldr: A balanced pilot and a positive-support exact-alpha main-wave mixture retain exact Horvitz--Thompson centering for the realized finite-population factorial vector.  The proved contribution is now an exact two-component risk identity, a first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain limit, and exclusion of the nearly-all-pilot endpoint.  The pilot likelihood factors exactly through revealed outcomes, but its realized information matrix need not converge to the population matrix under the current baseline assumptions.  A unique square-root pilot constant follows from a proved deterministic balanced-grid argmin proposition only if compact-window second-order convergence and endpoint coercivity are established.  Those statistical premises, including exact ties, unequal inclusions, arbitrary actions, and the nuisance-information bridge, remain open.

project_justification.gap: Existing factorial rerandomization theory supplies first-order Gaussian precision and existing two-wave work supplies accounting architecture, but neither proves a moving-boundary exact Horvitz--Thompson comparison at the square-root pilot scale.  The present information audit also shows that the stated moment conditions do not identify the pilot Fisher-information limit.
project_justification.niche: On a fixed complete baseline array with a full-dimensional product parameter domain, the design problem separates exactly into a deletion contrast and a potentially signed action-loss contrast.  This exposes, rather than assumes, the two finite-randomization bridges needed for sharp pilot sizing.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact pooled Horvitz--Thompson accounting, the explicit first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain coefficient, the exact pilot likelihood and realized information matrix, a nearly-all-pilot lower bound, and a conditional deterministic argmin certificate.  It leaves the frontier coefficients and the global statistical pilot theorem as explicit open questions.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on the selected pilot identities and balanced labels, only the revealed outcomes contribute to the likelihood.  Their score covariance is the random matrix \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\).  The current assumptions do not imply convergence of this matrix to \(I(\beta)\), so nuisance-efficient estimation and its transfer to exact action loss are conditional proof goals rather than established features.

prose_updates.related_work: Han and Deng provide the closest factorial sample-splitting architecture and first-order oracle equivalence; their results inform the present first-order comparison but do not supply the deletion cancellation or exact moving-boundary action loss.  Li and Ding provide the random-partition central limit theorem used for the bounded conditional-mean table.  Li, Ding, and Rubin provide the symmetric truncated-Gaussian predecessor, now recorded only as informing the unresolved finite-boundary question because the present design permits ties and unequal inclusions.  Yamin provides the deterministic compact-localization and argmin-transfer architecture, not the statistical square-root rate or its coefficients.  Armstrong's LAN efficiency bounds become relevant only after an actual pilot-information limit is available.  Horvitz and Thompson support exact inverse-inclusion centering, while the remaining rerandomization and consistency papers do not close the second-order exact-risk comparison.  Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella motivate sequential factorial replications, but no pilot-size recommendation is certified until the two open statistical premises are proved.
prose_updates.interpretation: For planning, the proved coefficient \(a(\beta)\) quantifies the first-order loss from deleting a macroscopic fraction of units for learning, and the nearly-all-pilot result rules out leaving only a sublinear main wave.  The familiar balance \(A t+B/t\) is presently a conditional design calculation, not a validated sample-size rule for this experiment.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact score orderings can jump on deterministic lattices and exact inclusion probabilities can be unequal.  The first-order proof absorbs these effects through zero Gaussian boundary mass, leave-one-unit inclusion convergence, and exact residual covariance cancellation.  These arguments do not provide the finer remainder needed when \(m/n\to0\).  Separately, smooth first and second outcome moments do not control score information as a function of the baseline, so the pilot LAN information cannot be fixed at \(I(\beta)\) without additional derivation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results are exact Horvitz--Thompson centering and accounting, the one-wave risk bound, common oracle-map convergence, Gaussian boundary regularity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle gain, the exact pilot likelihood and information audit, the nearly-all-pilot exclusion, and the conditional deterministic envelope transfer.  The coefficient \(A\) remains an unresolved deletion candidate and \(B\) remains a Gaussian action candidate.  Uniform frontier-scale deletion, exact finite action curvature, arbitrary-action localization, information convergence, the remaining endpoint windows, and the unconditional global pilot rule are open.  The causal estimand remains the fixed realized factorial vector throughout.
